context.label: Weeks, harvest, and the fiftieth day

observations.body: At Pentecost Tobit asks that a poor Israelite share his meal, learns of a murdered man in the street, carries the body away, and buries it after sunset despite neighbors’ ridicule.
observations.label: A Pentecost meal is interrupted by an unburied body

observations.body: The passage presents Inviting, carrying, and burying as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Inviting, carrying, and burying

observations.body: The passage places Tobit and Tobias beside Inviting, carrying, and burying.
observations.label: Tobit and Tobias

payload.posture: Read Tobit 2:1–8 as one movement in Pentecost, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states at Pentecost Tobit asks that a poor Israelite share his meal, learns of a murdered man in the street, carries the body away, and buries it after sunset despite neighbors’ ridicule. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Pentecost.
payload.title: A Pentecost meal is interrupted by an unburied body
